gates.what: Full mock, final speaking mock; the 6 Nov review sets Month 2

rules: Every piece of writing is marked within 24 hours and rewritten. Unmarked writing doesn't count.
All speaking homework is recorded. Listening back is half the exercise.
Timed means timed: phone in another room, no dictionary.
The error log is updated every day.
On a bad day the minimum is 45 minutes: one Part 2 recording, one reading passage, 10 minutes of error log. Never zero.
Sunday is off. Fatigue costs more than one rest day.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.intro: Get the speaking baseline, fix the structure of both writing tasks, and start the error log.

phases.name: Development
phases.intro: Longer, better-supported answers in speaking and writing, and the main reading question types under control. The week ends at the first checkpoint.

phases.name: Precision
phases.intro: Cut the errors: articles, collocations and templates out of the writing, and accuracy into the speaking.

phases.name: Test conditions
phases.intro: Everything timed, everything consistent. The week ends with a full re-baseline that decides Month 2.

questions.part1: Work: What do you do? What do you enjoy most about it? Is there anything you'd change about your job? · Mornings: Are you a morning person? What do you do first thing in the morning? Has your morning routine changed over the years? · Weather: What kind of weather do you like most? Does the weather affect your mood?
questions.part2: Describe a skill that took you a long time to learn. You should say: what the skill is, when and how you learned it, what made it difficult, and explain how you feel about it now.
questions.part3: Which skills matter most for young people today? Is it better to learn a skill from a teacher or online on your own? Why do some adults stop learning new things? How might the skills people need change in the next 20 years? Should schools teach more practical skills and fewer academic subjects?

prompts.text: Many young people change jobs several times in their first ten years of work. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?
Universities should only offer courses that lead directly to a job. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Some people think schools should teach children how to manage money, while others believe this is the family's job. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Many employees now work from home for part of the week. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
In many countries, fewer young people want to become teachers. Why is this, and what can be done about it?
Governments should spend more on public transport than on building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Some people say museums and galleries should be free to enter; others believe visitors should pay. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
More people now read online reviews before buying anything. Why is this? Is it a positive development?
More and more people choose to live alone. Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?
Top athletes are paid far more than their work is worth. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many working adults struggle to balance work and personal life. What causes this, and what can be done about it?
Some believe technology has brought people closer together; others think it has made them more isolated. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

errors.correct: Four paragraphs every time: introduction, two body paragraphs, a conclusion that restates your position
